caption: Vertafore at $5.35B against ~$590M of 2021 revenue and ~$290M of EBITDA: 9.1x forward revenue and 18.4x forward EBITDA, the entry price for the deal that made Roper a software company.
Frontline at $3.375B net of a ~$350M tax benefit, ~19x 2023E EBITDA on ~$370M of revenue, 90%+ recurring, net working capital at (40)% of revenue and unlevered free cash flow ~100% of EBITDA.
Deltek's 2023 share of each vertical it sells into: 39% of US government contracting and 69% of architecture and engineering, against 10% of construction SMB, 17% of consulting and 33% of creative.
Deltek after seven years of Roper ownership: revenue ~$500M to ~$800M, recurring revenue 70% to 82% of the total, EBITDA margin ~35% to ~40%, gross retention 93% to 97%.
Aderant's US share went from 31% in 2015 to 48% in 2022; 39 AmLaw 200 firms switched in from the largest competitor and none switched out over the prior decade.
Aderant after Roper: #2 to #1 in its market, revenue ~$100M to ~$200M, SaaS from 0% to 80% of bookings, net retention 102% to 113%, EBITDA margin 47% to 50%.
Verathon from 2014 to 2022: revenue ~$190M to ~$350M, organic growth low-single-digit to low-double-digit, and reoccurring consumable revenue from under 15% to 53% of the business.

Vertafore's penetration of P&C distribution: all 100 of the top 100 brokers buy something but only 66 run its agency management system, 96 of the top 100 carriers, ~85% of MGAs, and ~50% of producer-compliance transactions through Sircon.

Vertafore after Roper: revenue ~$550M to ~$635M, EBITDA margin 49% to 50%, gross and net retention 91%/105% to 92%/108%. The largest acquisition shows the smallest improvement of the four case studies.
DAT, acquired inside TransCore in 2004 and carved out internally, compounded pre-tax cash flow at 16% a year since acquisition. Roper's longest-dated disclosure of what one deal returned.

Strata, bought for $140M in 2015 with a $365M EPSi bolt-on in 2020: cash flow compounded 28% a year since acquisition, 23% excluding the bolt-on. The only case study that separates organic from acquired growth.
The acquisition funnel in one year: ~1,200 software targets, 235 reviewed, 93 NDAs, 71 management meetings, 25 indications of interest, 16 full diligences, 6 closings.

Net debt to EBITDA from Q4'16 to Q4'22: every leverage peak (4.2x for Deltek, 4.7x for Vertafore) followed an acquisition and was repaid within two years. The 3.4x reached in Q2'26 followed a buyback.

The published long-term algorithm: double-digit revenue growth, mid-single-digit-plus organic, 45%+ operating leverage and mid-teens free cash flow compounding. FY2025 converted 36% of incremental revenue to EBITDA and FY2026 is guided to 8%+ revenue growth.

CentralReach at $1.65B net of a $200M tax benefit for ~$175M of revenue and ~$75M of EBITDA: 9.4x revenue and 22x EBITDA, the highest earnings multiple of the three disclosed deals, paid for a 20%+ grower.

Capital allocation after the break: 3.4x net leverage, $2.9B drawn on a $3.5B revolver, $365M of cash, 9.0M shares (over 8% of the company) repurchased for $3.2B, and $1.4B of expected Indicor proceeds.
